cases.prompt: Define release gates for hot-plug recovery, firmware update, monitor mapping, installer compatibility and operator usability.
required_behaviors: recognizes measurable reliability, compatibility, usability, security and maintainability scenarios
forbidden_behaviors: uses subjective labels such as user-friendly without measures
baseline_expected_failure: agent lists ISO characteristics without system scenarios
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Turn remote-update reliability into measurable acceptance and release evidence.
required_behaviors: defines stimulus, environment, response and measure
defines pass threshold and evidence source
includes restart, partial failure and rollback cases
connects defects to a release decision
baseline_expected_failure: agent produces metrics unrelated to failure consequences
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Tell me the names of the ISO/IEC 25010 quality characteristics with no product context.
required_behaviors: answers as a reference question or asks for context before defining gates
forbidden_behaviors: pretends a release gate can be defined without a system
baseline_expected_failure: agent applies a full project quality process to a terminology request
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Define release gates for a config-driven distributed equipment prototype moving from simulated IO to real chamber hardware.
required_behaviors: defines reliability, compatibility, performance, security, maintainability and usability scenarios with measures
distinguishes simulated, multi-process, multi-PC and real-hardware evidence
includes command/readback, disconnect, restart, schema mismatch and rollback cases
forbidden_behaviors: uses a generic checklist without thresholds or owners
treats demo success as full release evidence
baseline_expected_failure: agent lists ISO characteristics but no executable evidence
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Define release evidence for a real-time native application whose emulator tests pass but whose decisions combine asynchronous sensor and command results on several supported builds.
required_behaviors: defines freshness, timestamp-domain, correlation and maximum-skew criteria at the decision point
preserves denominators and reports stale, missing, duplicate and out-of-order samples separately
distinguishes emulator evidence from native platform, architecture, build-mode and hardware evidence
defines a risk-based release matrix with explicit unsupported cells, owners and hard or conditional gates
forbidden_behaviors: uses average latency alone to prove real-time alignment
treats emulator success as evidence for native ABI, timing or device behavior
silently removes failing or unexecuted matrix cells from the denominator
baseline_expected_failure: agent reports throughput and emulator pass rate without decision-time correlation or native matrix evidence
cases.review_notes: Use system-specific thresholds supplied by the project; do not invent timing or safety limits.

cases.prompt: Improve tests for a simulator supporting one or two transfer resources, fixed and parallel modes, two input sides, and recipes with unequal durations.
required_behaviors: Cover both input sides rather than proving only the first side moves.
Include resource overlap, same-side return, unequal-duration progress, buffer priority, and repeated carrier-cycle assertions.
forbidden_behaviors: Claim a mode works from a single happy-path side.
Correlate reused carrier identifiers as one object forever.
required_artifacts: a minimal scenario matrix covering both input sides, resource overlap, same-side return, unequal-duration progress, buffer priority, and repeated carrier-cycle assertions
a scenario protecting the previously-stable single-resource path from regression
baseline_expected_failure: agent claims a mode works from a single happy-path side only, or correlates reused carrier identifiers as if they were one object forever
